clusters.representative_signature: NOC_TIMEOUT | NOC: Transaction timeout ; NOC: NoC error register snapshot ; SYSTEM: Interconnect failure ; NOC: Fabric <*> ; NOC: DMA burst overflow

hypotheses.root_cause: A DMA burst on channel 2 (burst_len=256) overran the fabric buffers. This congested the paths to DDR, and a PCIE->DDR transaction (0xB691) then timed out, causing the fatal interconnect failure.
hypotheses.rationale: Pulling only the WARN/ERROR lines for the whole run (0-3546 ms) shows the catalogue tell-tale for RC_DMA_BURST_OVERFLOW: 'NOC: WARN: DMA burst overflow | channel=2 burst_len=256' at 2882 ms, about 560 ms before the first error. Four high-occupancy congestion warnings follow (CPU<->DDR and CPU<->PCIE, stall_pct 25-31%), and then the PCIE->DDR transaction timeout at 3444 ms. A DMA->DDR buffer overrun fits that sequence. The tell-tales for the other catalogue causes are absent: no 'QoS credit starvation/credits=0' and no 'Dependency cycle suspected'. Those are the markers that identified the high-similarity past incidents 000003 (QoS starvation) and 000021 (deadlock), so those signature matches look superficial. The NOC0 register dump is raw hex with no decoded fields and adds nothing. Confounder: the PCIe link retrain count climbs steadily (36->41) across the error window with aer=0. A flaky PCIe link could also stall the PCIE-sourced transaction. This is why my confidence is moderate rather than high. Thermal, PMU and DDR telemetry are all normal (ecc_ue=0, read latency 72-84 ns).
recommended_actions: Rerun the same workload with the DMA channel 2 burst length reduced (e.g. 64/128) and/or an outstanding-transaction limit. Check whether the congestion warnings and the timeout go away.
Check the buffer depth on the DMA->DDR fabric path against burst_len=256, and capture NoC buffer-occupancy counters around the overflow event.
Rule out the PCIe link: find out why the retrain count keeps increasing (36->41). Rerun with the link fixed at Gen3 x16 with equalization checked, and see whether the PCIE->DDR timeout still happens.
Decode the NOC0 error register snapshot (0x60000BDC-0x60000C28) against the register map to confirm the failing initiator and buffer-overflow status bits.
